newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia to convert military base to cargo airport.
newsitem.headline: Russia to convert military base to cargo airport.

text.p: Russia plans to convert a military air base in Leningrad region into an international cargo airport by the year 2000, a local official said on Tuesday.
Sergei Skripnikov, a head of the international projects department in the Leningrad region administration, told Reuters the project would cost about $250 million.
He said it planned to get Western loans to set up the airport named as Veshchevo, 150 km north-west of St Petersburg, near the Russian-Finnish border.

"The Netherlands Economics Institute (NEI) is preparing documents and will find bank loans for the project later," Skripnikov said. The NEI is funded by the Dutch goverment which has an agreement with the Leningrad region administration.
The region around St Petersburg is still called Leningrad and is administratively separate from the city.
Skripnikov said the new airport would service all types of freighters.
"Experts said that the new airport may be profitable because Pulkovo international airport in St Petersburg operates only passenger flights," he said.
